text: {"final": {"verdict": "accept", "reason": "The script matches the code and the ticket. delivery_status() returns the gateway's status map (new messages have no entry, so they can't be in the failed set); sent_messages() returns SmsMessage objects with id, household_id, template_id and params, all of which the script uses correctly. queue_sms(household_id, template_id, params) re-renders from the approved template and appends to the outbox itself, so the script never touches data/outbox/sms.jsonl directly. The failed set (SMS-00001/04/05/06/09/10/12/18/19/20) covers distinct households, and the resent-households guard ensures exactly one resend per household even if a household had multiple failures; delivered households are never in the failed set so they are not texted. The sys.path.insert and docstring follow the scripts/stock_report.py pattern, and the docstring states it sends SMS messages as required."}}
reasoning:
Check the script logic. Failed ids: SMS-00001, 04, 05, 06, 09, 10, 12, 18, 19, 20. Each failed message is a distinct household, so the dedup set doesn't skip anything. Script re-queues with template_id and params — correct. queue_sms checks sms_ok; if a household hasn't agreed to SMS, it would raise. But original messages were sent, so presumably sms_ok. The script follows stock_report pattern, docstring says sends SMS. New messages have no status entry — but the script iterates sent_messages() and only re-queues those in failed set; new messages queued during the run would have no status entry and not be in failed set, so ignored. Correct.

One subtlety: queue_sms computes next id from sent_messages() which reads the outbox each time — fine. The script doesn't read outbox directly. All good. Accept.
